keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1054-1055: Cliopatria's first Kiev shape is 1056, but the Kievan Rus' page gives 'Principality of Kiev and Novgorod, for the eldest son Iziaslav I of Kiev' in the division 'after the death of Yaroslav I in 1054', and the rus dossier hands the land over in 1054. The 1056 shape is used.

146,800 km2 on both banks of the Dnieper from the Pripyat (Turov and Pinsk) to the steppe edge, west to 25.4 E. The page: 'the inner principality covered land on both banks of the Dnieper', bordering Polotsk (north-west), Chernigov (north-east), Poland (west), Galicia (south-west) and Cumania (south-east). The Council of Liubech page (19 October 1097) gives Sviatopolk II 'Kiev, Turov and Pinsk', which supports the Pripyat side being in this shape. Infobox gives no area, so nothing to compare.
146,700 km2: 1056 shape (50 vertices to 61), area -46 km2 only. No page event.

147,700 km2: two cells added at 27.4-27.6 E, 53.4 N; no page event. The Polotsk dossier has Mstislav of Kiev annexing Polotsk in 1129 and losing it in 1132; no Kiev shape shows it.

147,400 km2, the shape unchanged in effect. The page: in '1150-1180: Vyshhorod, Kaniv, and Belgorod "sought independence as individual principalities"', which Cliopatria does not draw separately; Yuri Dolgorukiy held Kiev 1149-1151 and 1155-1157 (the rostov-suzdal dossier records these as occupations; mirrored here).

78,100 km2: the Pripyat side (296 cells, 25.5-30.6 E, 51.1-53.4 N; 295 are the 295 of 297 cells of Cliopatria's Turov and Pinsk shape of 1188) leaves the Kiev shape. The Turov page puts Turov's 'full independence from Kievan Rus'' in 1162 ('Finally in 1162 the principality was passed by Yuri Dolgoruki back to one of the Izyaslavichi') and gives no 1188 event; the principality-of-turov-and-pinsk dossier founds the state in 1188 on the same land. Kept so the two dossiers agree; ledger loss confidence 1.

78,400 km2 for 1202-1235 (Kiev, Vyshhorod, Kaniv, Belgorod). The page's list: Mstislav Romanovich 1214-1223, Vladimir IV Rurikovich 1223-1235; no frontier event. The galicia-volhynia dossier records Roman's hold on Kiev in 1200-1205 and Daniel's protection in 1239.

78,400 km2 for 1236-1240. The Mongol invasion page: 'The Mongols approach on Kiev in November 1240' and 'the horde stormed Kiev in December 1240'; 'Prince Daniel had taken Kiev under his protection the previous year'. Cliopatria ends the shape in 1240.

ledger.note: 1054: Yaroslav's death gives Kiev and Novgorod to his eldest son Iziaslav I, who becomes grand prince. Kievan Rus' page: 'Principality of Kiev and Novgorod, for the eldest son Iziaslav I of Kiev, who became grand prince'; Yaroslav died on 20 February 1054 (Yaroslav the Wise page infobox). Cliopatria's shape begins in 1056.

1132: Mstislav I dies and the semi-autonomous states become de facto independent; Kiev is one principality among them. Page: the principality emerged 'after Mstislav I's death in 1132, when the semi-autonomous states were de facto independent' (infobox 'Established: 1132'). The Kievan Rus' page: 'After his death in 1132, Kievan Rus' fell into recession and a rapid decline.' No border change.

ledger.note: 1188: the Pripyat side leaves the Kiev shape as the principality of Turov and Pinsk (Cliopatria). The Turov page puts Turov's independence from Kievan Rus' in 1162, not 1188; year is Cliopatria's, matching the principality-of-turov-and-pinsk dossier.
November 1240: the Mongols approach Kiev. 'The Mongols approach on Kiev in November 1240'.

December 1240: the Mongols storm Kiev. 'the horde stormed Kiev in December 1240'; the infobox: 'Destruction of Kiev by Batu Khan: 1240'; the invasion left the principality 'in a severely ruined state' with 'only about 200 houses left'. The page gives no day (the mongol-empire dossier has 6 December from a different page).

December 1240: Batu destroys Kiev and the principality ends as a state of its own; its principalities 'became part of the Jochid appanage ruled by Batu'. The Kiev page continues the principality to 1471 under suzerains; the year of the end is the page's, the reading as the state's end is the researcher's and Cliopatria's.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Kievan Rus'
wars.outcome: Mongols storm Kiev in December 1240 after Daniel of Galicia, who had taken Kiev under his protection in 1239, withdrew to defend Galicia-Volhynia; the principalities become a Jochid appanage under Batu and the Mongol supremacy lasts into the 14th century.
wars.note: Prince Michael of Kiev fled after first resisting; the page names no Kiev defender other than Daniel's voivode (page silent on Dmitr).

wars.name: Battle of the Alta River
wars.outcome: Defeat of Yaroslav's sons by the Cumans; Iziaslav fled to Poland and returned 'in a couple of years'. No territory changed.
wars.note: The page gives the year in 'the 1068 defeat by the Cumans at the Battle of the Alta River' and no month; it does not say where the Alta lies.

certainty.note: River, forest and steppe frontiers never fixed by treaty; the 1097 Council of Liubech assigns lands to princes without boundaries. The Pripyat (Turov-Pinsk) side is soft in particular: Turov separates in 1162 by the page, 1188 by Cliopatria.

notes:
Start 1054, not the page's 1132: the Principality of Kiev infobox says 'Established: 1132'; Cliopatria draws the shape from 1056 and the rus dossier (eu-16-a) ends in 1054 and hands Kiev over with the sons' principalities. 1132 is a rename event. Likewise the page runs the principality to 1471 (Kiev Voivodeship of Lithuania after Simeon Olelkovich) under suzerains: Vladimir 1243-1271, Galicia-Volhynia 1271-1301, Golden Horde 1301-1362, Lithuania 1362-1471. This dossier ends in December 1240 with Cliopatria's last shape; the later centuries belong to the suzerains' dossiers (mongol-empire/golden-horde, grand-duchy-of-lithuania).

Turov and Pinsk: Kiev's shape loses the Pripyat side in 1188 (Cliopatria). The Turov page says full independence from Kievan Rus' came in 1162. The loss is dated 1188, confidence 1, to agree with the principality-of-turov-and-pinsk dossier (eu-16-e), whose note makes the same observation; moving both to 1162 would be the page-faithful fix.

Not written because no page opened dates it: Mstislav's war on Polotsk (1127-1129) and the loss in 1132, which the principality-of-polotsky dossier (eu-16-c) records against this state (contest 1127-1129, loss 1129, gain 1132; the Kiev shape shows no change). The Roman 1200-1205 and Daniel 1239-1240 holds on Kiev are vassal events in the principality-of-galicia-volhynia dossier (suzerain side), as are the Mongol vassal_start in 1240 in the mongol-empire dossier. The 1169 sack by Andrey Bogolyubsky and the 1203 sack by Rurik and the Cumans are not on the page. Vyshhorod, Kaniv and Belgorod 'sought independence' 1150-1180 (undated by year, no shape change).

The prince table was read from the page's list as extracted; the page's own table overlaps in 1167-1171 and 1177-1194 and lists Sviatoslav Vsevolodovich 'of Vladimir' for 1177-1194 and Rurik Rostislavich in 1180-1181 inside it, which may be errors in the page's table; kept as the page gives them. Months for Yuri Dolgorukiy's two tenures come from the Rostov-Suzdal dossier and are not repeated here.
